title: Convert a decimal string to int safely
description: Write a function `string_to_int_matches(text, target)` that tries `int(text)` and returns whether it equals `target` - and returns `False` (instead of crashing) if `text` can't be converted directly, e.g. `'9.8'`.
hints: Idea to consider: int() can't parse a string that contains a decimal point
int('9.8') raises a ValueError - int() only accepts strings that look like whole numbers, unlike float() which accepts a decimal point.
Wrap int(text) in a try/except ValueError - on success compare it to target, on failure return False.
expected_behavior: Returns whether int(text) equals target, or False if text can't be parsed as an int.
explanation: int('9.8') doesn't round or truncate - it refuses to parse a decimal point at all, which is different from float(), and worth catching explicitly rather than assuming int() always succeeds on a numeric-looking string.
